Our company is organizing a team-building cooking workshop next month and I need you to prepare the materials. We want to feature three Chinese dishes that are relatively easy to make (rated as easy, i.e. a low difficulty score, in the recipe database), and cover different categories so we get some variety. Please search through the available recipe database to find three suitable dishes that meet these criteria.

Note: write all document content in English (dish names, ingredients, cooking steps, tips, and the shopping list).

Once you have selected the three recipes, I need you to create three deliverables in the workspace.

First, create a Word document called Workshop_Handbook.docx. This should serve as a detailed step-by-step cooking guide for participants. Start with a title "Cooking Workshop Handbook" as a top-level heading. Then for each of the three dishes, include a second-level heading with the dish name, followed by a paragraph listing all the required ingredients with quantities, and then another paragraph (or multiple paragraphs) walking through the cooking steps in order. At the end of the document, add a section called "Tips and Notes" with any general cooking advice that would help beginners.

Second, create a PowerPoint presentation called Workshop_Slides.pptx for the instructor to use during the workshop. The first slide should be a title slide with "Team Cooking Workshop" as the title. Then for each dish, create two slides: one slide with the dish name as the title and the ingredient list as the content, and a second slide with the dish name followed by "Steps" as the title and the cooking steps as bullet points. Finally add a closing slide with "Enjoy Your Meal!" as the title.

Third, create a PDF file called Shopping_List.pdf in the workspace. This should be a consolidated shopping list that combines all ingredients from all three dishes, organized neatly so that someone from our procurement team can use it to go shopping. Group similar ingredients together if possible and include the total quantities needed. The document should have a clear title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" at the top.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must first query the exact `早餐`, `素菜`, and `主食` category listings in one native-parallel response, select one low-difficulty candidate ID from each category, and retrieve the three exact-ID recipe details in a second native-parallel response. Require three distinct IDs/categories and source-supported low difficulty, then freeze each recipe's English name, full translated ingredients with quantities, ordered translated steps, and beginner tips. The three independent deliverables can then be created in one wave.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Handbook.docx and writes the exact title, one complete section for each of the three frozen dishes, ordered ingredients/steps, and Tips and Notes. Read it back and return its path and three-dish coverage checks.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Slides.pptx and creates exactly the title slide, two slides for each of the three frozen dishes, and the Enjoy Your Meal closing slide. Read it back and return its path, presentation ID, eight-slide count, titles, and dish coverage.

   3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 2): One coder sub-agent owns Shopping_List.pdf and consolidates all ingredients from the same three frozen recipes in English with combined quantities and clear grouping. Read it back and return its path, title, ingredient coverage, and quantity controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent must cross-check the same three dishes and ingredients across all deliverables and finish without another wave.

You are building a Word document deliverable for a company team-building cooking workshop. Everything must be written in English.

WORKSPACE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace
Output file (absolute path): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Workshop_Handbook.docx

Use the mcp__word__* tools to create and fill the document (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.). All text content must be English. Do not invent new ingredients or steps beyond what is given below.

=== FROZEN RECIPE CONTENT (use exactly this, translated to English as given) ===

DISH 1: Pan-Fried Dumplings (category: Breakfast; difficulty: Easy)
Ingredients:
- Frozen dumplings: 1 pack (about 10-15 pieces per person)
- Cooking oil: 10-15 ml
- Black sesame seeds: a pinch (for garnish)
- Scallions: a small handful, chopped (for garnish)
- Water: as needed for steaming (tap water, no purchase needed)
Steps:
1. Take out a frying pan (a non-stick pan is best).
2. Add 10-15 ml of cooking oil.
3. Turn on the heat and place the dumplings in the pan, spread out evenly (do not stack them).
4. Immediately add water until the waterline reaches about half the average height of the dumplings.
5. Cover with a lid (the stove should be on high heat).
6. Wait 8-10 minutes.
7. When only about 2 mm of water remains in the pan, turn to medium heat and start pan-frying.
8. When all the water has evaporated, shake the pan gently so the dumplings heat evenly.
9. Sprinkle in black sesame seeds and chopped scallions, cover and steam for 10 seconds.
10. After 1-2 minutes, take one dumpling out to check the bottom; once a golden crispy crust appears, remove all dumplings from the pan and serve.

DISH 2: Stir-Fried Tomatoes and Eggs (category: Vegetable; difficulty: Easy)
Ingredients (per serving):
- Tomatoes: 1 (about 180 g)
- Eggs: 2 (the recipe calls for 1.5 per serving, rounded up)
- Cooking oil: about 8 ml (4 ml per egg)
- Salt: 1.5-2 g
- Sugar (optional): 0-2 g
- Chopped scallions (optional): 0-10 g
Steps:
1. Wash the tomatoes.
2. Optional: peel the tomatoes (remove the outer skin).
3. Remove the stems and cut the tomatoes into small pieces no larger than 4 cm - these are the "tomato pieces".
4. Crack the eggs into a bowl, add 1 g of salt (per serving), and whisk until well combined - this is the "egg mixture".
5. Heat the wok and add the cooking oil.
6. When the oil is hot, pour in the egg mixture and stir-fry until the eggs set into solids and turn slightly golden - these are the "half-cooked eggs".
7. Turn off the heat, plate the half-cooked eggs, then turn the heat back on.
8. Add the tomato pieces, press with the spatula and stir-fry for about 20 seconds, or until the tomatoes soften and break down.
9. Return the half-cooked eggs to the wok and stir-fry to combine everything evenly.
10. Add the remaining salt, sugar (optional, if you prefer a sweeter version), and chopped scallions (optional), and stir-fry to combine.
11. Turn off the heat, transfer to a plate, and serve.

DISH 3: Scallion Oil Noodles (category: Staple; difficulty: Easy)
Ingredients (per serving):
- Scallions: 100 g
- Cooking oil: 100 ml
- Light soy sauce: 60 ml
- Dark soy sauce: 20 ml
- White sugar: 15 g
- Dried noodles: 80 g (about 150 g of fresh/wet noodles)
- Water: 1000 ml for boiling (tap water, no purchase needed)
- Prepared scallion oil sauce: 15 ml per serving (made in step 6)
Steps:
1. Wash the scallions and cut them into long sections (about 5-7 cm). You can separate the white parts from the green parts.
2. Add 100 ml of cooking oil to a pan and heat over medium heat. First add the white scallion sections and stir-fry until they turn slightly yellow.
3. Add the green scallion sections, turn the heat to low, and continue stir-frying.
4. Keep the heat low and stir-fry patiently for about 15-20 minutes, until the scallion sections turn golden and crispy.
5. Remove the crispy golden scallion sections from the oil (keep the scallion-flavored oil in the pan).
6. To the scallion oil in the pan, add 60 ml light soy sauce, 20 ml dark soy sauce, and 15 g white sugar. Heat over low heat and stir for about 1 minute until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is well mixed. Turn off the heat immediately. Pour the scallion oil sauce into a container and let it cool; it can be stored sealed.
7. Take 80 g of dried noodles.
8. Add 1000 ml of drinking water to a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
9. Add the noodles and cook until done according to the package instructions (usually 3-8 minutes).
10. Remove the cooked noodles, drain well, and place them in a bowl.
11. Add 15 ml of the prepared scallion oil sauce to the noodles in the bowl.
12. Optionally top with the fried crispy scallion sections.
13. Toss everything quickly with chopsticks until well coated, then serve.

=== REQUIRED DOCUMENT STRUCTURE ===
1. Top-level heading (Heading 1): "Cooking Workshop Handbook"
2. For EACH of the three dishes, in this order (Pan-Fried Dumplings, then Stir-Fried Tomatoes and Eggs, then Scallion Oil Noodles):
   - A second-level heading (Heading 2) with the dish name (e.g., "Pan-Fried Dumplings").
   - A paragraph labeled "Ingredients:" that lists all the ingredients with their quantities (one ingredient per line).
   - One or more paragraphs labeled "Steps:" that walk through the cooking steps in order (numbered 1, 2, 3, ...).
3. At the end, a second-level heading "Tips and Notes" followed by general beginner cooking advice. Use these tips (write each as its own line/paragraph):
   - Read each recipe all the way through and prepare all ingredients and tools before you start cooking.
   - Keep the heat lower than you think you need; it is easier to turn it up than to rescue burnt food.
   - Use a non-stick pan whenever possible - it makes pan-frying dumplings and cooking eggs much easier.
   - Have a lid ready when frying dumplings so you can steam them without oil splattering.
   - Taste as you go and season gradually; you can always add more salt or sugar, but you cannot take it out.
   - When cutting scallions, keep your fingers curled with your knuckles against the blade for safety.
   - Cut tomatoes into even-sized pieces so they cook evenly.
   - For the scallion oil, be patient: low heat and time create the fragrant golden scallions. Do not rush with high heat or they will burn and taste bitter.
   - Clean up as you go to keep the workspace tidy and safe.
   - When in doubt, follow the package instructions for noodles and dumplings - cooking times vary by brand.

=== VERIFICATION (REQUIRED) ===
After creating the document, read it back with get_document_text (or equivalent) and verify:
(a) the title "Cooking Workshop Handbook" appears,
(b) all three dish sections are present with their headings,
(c) the "Tips and Notes" section exists,
(d) ingredients and numbered steps are present for each dish.
Fix any issues you find.

=== RETURN CONTRACT ===
Return a concise report containing:
1. The absolute path of the saved file.
2. Confirmation of (a)-(d) with short evidence (e.g., extracted title and heading list).
3. A list of the three dish names covered.
Do not create any other files.
